newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 21.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 21.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
** Indian shares seen sharply higher as Inder Kumar Gujral is named India's prime minister on Sunday, ending a three-week political crisis that rocked financial markets and paralysed the government

** President Shankar Dayal Sharma asks Gujral to form a new government after the Congress party, which had sparked the upheaval but feared snap polls, renewed its support for the centre-left United Front coalition
** Gujral must prove his majority in the lower house of parliament by Tuesday. He is to be sworn in at 10 a.m. (0430 GMT) on Monday along with his council of ministers
** The United Front says it is confident that outgoing Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will retain his job in a new government and push the 1997/98 budget through parliament
"I am confident that Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will pilot the Finance Bill through parliament," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy says

** Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress party has vowed not to join the new government. TMC leader G.K. Moopanar had been a leading contender to succeed caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who resigned on April 11 after losing a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament
** Gujral faces a confidence vote on Tuesday at 11:00 a.m. (0530 GMT). Indian parties will set a timetable for the 1997/98 budget later in the day, a government official says
** Analysts say Indian markets' relief that the United Front has found a new leader will turn to despair if Chidambaram does not return to the Finance Ministry
Most analysts expect stock markets to open stronger on Monday out of sheer relief that mid-term polls are put off at least a little while longer
** Shares of India's largest private firm Reliance Industries seen in the limelight ahead of its financial results for 1996/97 (April-March) due on Tuesday
** Reliance shares are expected to open sharply higher due to higher bookclosure carry forward charges of 8.80 rupees per share as the share enters a no-delivery period on the Bombay bourse.
** Most Indian stock markets remained closed for a Moslem holiday on Friday
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index jumped 49.08 points, or 1.35 percent, to end at 3696.52 on Thursday. The National index climbed 20.50 points, or 2.02 percent, to 1035.40
